message_source_quote: The white-bear steering paper (Raman et al., 2026, in the reading list) solves this exact setup using WorkspaceBench's own `directed_modulation` items at a bench-chosen dose. I instead built an *independently authored, self-contained* stance contrast that uses no bench family.
writeup_source_quote: A stance direction built from WorkspaceBench's own `directed_modulation` pairs was shown to lift association (Raman et al., 2026). Our contribution: the stance direction is *robust to the contrast source*.
rationale: Both documents explicitly name Raman et al., 2026 ("white-bear steering") as the prior work that built a stance/contrast direction from WorkspaceBench's own directed_modulation pairs/items at a bench-chosen dose, and both frame the present method's novelty identically: an independently authored, bench-free contrast that recovers a direction at cosine 0.81 to the bench-derived one and outperforms it (0.76 vs 0.69), demonstrating the stance direction is robust to the contrast source. The message makes no additional claims about the contents of the write-up document itself beyond describing the method and results, so there is nothing to check for misdescription, and no material difference in source attribution, overlap, or novelty framing exists between the two documents.
